about: CafeMS risk register. Components are rated with the Weighted Security Exposure Score (Low 1, Medium 3, High 5; weights: accessibility 2, data sensitivity 3, past incidents 2, complexity 1). Failure modes are rated with FMEA (Severity x Occurrence x Detection, each 1-10). 'before' is the prototype as audited on 2026-11-04; 'after' is the current code. Past incidents count defects found in our own audits, since the cafe has no production history. Every 'tests' entry names a test in tests/ that proves the control. Scores are worked out by server/lib/risk.js, never typed in.

components.name: Sign-in, MFA and sessions
components.why: Reachable from the internet and holds password hashes and MFA secrets, so exposure stays high. The prototype accepted any password; the review found MFA guessing without lockout, now fixed. MFA, enrolment and recovery codes make it more complex than before.

components.name: Whole-database API (/api/state)
components.why: Removed in Phase 1. Every read and write now goes through a guarded, validated route.

components.name: Billing, payments and refunds
components.why: Staff only, but it moves money and holds customer numbers. The review found a possible double payment and cashier access to old bills, both fixed.
controls: Refunds need an authenticator code; large refunds a second person

components.name: Staff accounts and roles
components.why: Only Admins reach it now, after an authenticator re-check. No defect was found in the review.

components.name: Audit log
components.why: Admin read-only. The review found actions that could be saved without their entry, now fixed.
controls: Written in the same transaction as the action
Database account cannot change or delete entries

components.name: Orders and kitchen
components.why: Orders hold no customer data, and the kitchen gets no prices. No defect was found in the review.
controls: Waiters see only their own orders

components.name: Reservations
components.why: Holds guest names and numbers, encrypted. The review found new bookings hidden behind old ones and erased bookings that could reopen, both fixed.
controls: AES-256-GCM for name, phone and notes

components.name: Public website and online booking
components.why: Anyone can reach it, and online booking now collects a name and number.
controls: Same answer whether or not a booking existed

components.name: Inventory
components.why: Only Managers change stock; Admins can view it. Stock can never go below zero.

components.name: MongoDB database
components.why: Listens on this computer only and now requires a login; the app account is least privilege. It ran without a login until the review.

failureModes.effect: Anyone can act as any member of staff
failureModes.action: Argon2id check on the server, mandatory MFA, failed sign-ins recorded and alerted
tests: a wrong password is refused, even though it meets the rules (finding 1)
a correct password alone gives no session (MFA is mandatory)
failed sign-ins, denials, exports, number views and refunds each raise an alert

failureModes.failure: Database read or replaced without signing in
failureModes.effect: All customer, staff and financial data exposed or wiped
failureModes.action: Whole-database routes removed; every route guarded and checked by a test
tests: the old whole-database routes are gone (findings 2, 3)
every route has a guard, so none can be left open by accident (complete mediation)

failureModes.effect: A user sees or changes data that belongs to someone else
failureModes.action: Server permission matrix on every route, ownership in every query, denials audited and alerted
tests: every role against every route (RBAC matrix)
one waiter cannot see or change another waiter's order
a denied page is recorded

failureModes.failure: Bill total or quantity tampered with
failureModes.action: Totals worked out on the server from stored prices; strict schemas refuse extra fields
tests: the total is calculated on the server; the browser cannot set it (Rs 2,500 to 250)
negative, zero, fractional, huge and non-numeric quantities are refused

failureModes.failure: Two screens save at once and one change is lost
failureModes.action: Transactions, version checks and atomic stock updates
tests: an edit from an out-of-date screen is refused rather than overwriting
simultaneous orders cannot both take the last portion

failureModes.failure: Audit log edited without anyone noticing
failureModes.effect: Fraud or misuse cannot be proved
failureModes.action: Signed SHA-256 chain, verified every 15 minutes with an alert; app account cannot edit entries
tests: detects edited details, a changed actor and a changed time
detects a recalculated hash, because the attacker cannot sign it
the app account can add audit entries but cannot change or delete them

failureModes.effect: Bill stuck, or a customer never hears back
failureModes.action: 3-second gateway timeout to Pending Payment with retry; notification outbox with retries and an Admin alert
tests: a timeout leaves the bill Pending Payment, the till responsive and revenue unchanged
failures retry with growing gaps, then raise one Admin alert

failureModes.failure: Double click creates a duplicate order
failureModes.effect: Extra food made and stock taken
failureModes.action: Idempotency key on every order, payment and refund
tests: a double click creates one order and takes stock once
a double click produces one bill

failureModes.failure: Authenticator codes guessed without a lockout
failureModes.effect: An attacker with a stolen password gets in
failureModes.action: Failure count clears only after the full sign-in; alert on many failures from one address
tests: the right password alone does not reset the count, so authenticator codes cannot be guessed forever
one password tried against many usernames from one address raises an alert (password spraying)

failureModes.action: No second payment during a charge; a late approval is recorded and alerted
tests: no second payment is taken while a card charge is still waiting for the gateway
a late approval for a bill already paid another way is recorded and raises an alert

failureModes.failure: An action is saved without its audit entry
failureModes.effect: A change happens that nobody can trace
failureModes.action: Every change commits in the same transaction as its entry
tests: if the audit entry fails, the action it describes does not happen
an action that cannot be recorded does not happen (fail-secure audit)
